en: The Apadāna of the Elder Caṅkoṭakiya Suvaṇṇabibbohana Chapter 3 I was a king named Mahinda, ruling over the earth. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, the Teacher of the World, appeared in the world. Having heard of the Buddha’s arrival, I went to him with great joy. Approaching the Teacher, I paid homage at his feet. Then I requested of the Buddha, the Great Sage: “May the Blessed One, out of compassion for me, accept a meal from me tomorrow. The Teacher, the Great Sage, accepted my invitation. Having made the request, I returned to my own palace. That very night, I prepared a vast array of food and drink. When the morning had dawned, I had the city decorated. I had the streets swept clean and sprinkled with scented water. I had banners and flags raised everywhere. Then, having prepared a seat for the Teacher, I invited the Teacher, the Great Sage, saying: “May the Blessed One come; may the Sugata enter. The Teacher, the Great Sage, entered the city. He sat upon the seat prepared for him. Having seated himself, he spoke these words: “O King, bring the food and drink quickly. Hearing the Teacher’s words, I brought the food and drink. With my own hands, I served the Teacher, the Great Sage. Having satisfied the Teacher with food and drink, I bowed my head and stood before him. Then the Teacher, the Great Sage, spoke these words: “O King, listen to what I have to say. In the future, after a long time has passed, there will be a Buddha named Metteyya. He will appear in the world as the Teacher of the World. At that time, you shall become his chief disciple, known by the name of Culla-Panthaka. Hearing the Teacher’s words, I was filled with joy. I paid homage at the Teacher’s feet and departed. Because of that deed, I experienced happiness for a long time. For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms. I was always born in the heavens and among humans. Now, having reached this final existence, I am an Arhat. Through the power of that former deed, I have attained this state. Thus did I perform that meritorious deed. This is the account of the Elder Caṅkoṭakiya.
“Dwelling between the mountains, he relies upon the great ocean;
having gone out to meet him and paid him honor, [he said:]”
[the dwelling] of the Great Seer Siddhattha,
who has compassion for all beings.
may I rejoice in heaven for an eon;
I then gave a bamboo basket;
I do not know a state of misery—
this is the fruit of that bamboo basket.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so on]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Caṅkoṭakiya spoke these verses.
This is the third legend of the elder Caṅkoṭakiya.
